items.stem: For a one-parameter exponential family with a monotone likelihood ratio, a UMP test is generally available for which alternative?
options: A one-sided alternative in the appropriate direction
items.explanation: The monotone likelihood ratio property supports a UMP test for a one-sided alternative in the corresponding direction. A single UMP test generally does not exist for a two-sided alternative.

items.stem: The likelihood ratio statistic is defined as the supremum of the likelihood under the null divided by the supremum under:
items.explanation: The denominator maximises the likelihood over the full parameter space, which contains the null parameter space. Consequently the likelihood ratio lies between zero and one.

items.stem: Let X have density 1/θ on 0 ≤ x ≤ θ. A test rejects H₀: θ=1 when X≥0.25. What is its power at θ=2?
items.explanation: Under θ=2, X is uniform on [0,2]. Thus Pθ=2(X≥0.25)=(2−0.25)/2=0.875.

items.topic: Power of tests for a uniform model
items.stem: For X ~ Uniform(0,θ), a test rejects when X≥c, where 0<c<1. Its size under H₀: θ=1 is:
items.explanation: Under the null, X is uniform on [0,1]. Therefore the rejection probability is P(X≥c)=1−c, which is the size.

items.stem: For a sample x₁,…,xₙ from an exponential distribution with rate λ, the maximum likelihood estimator of λ is:
items.explanation: The log-likelihood is n log λ−λΣxᵢ. Setting its derivative n/λ−Σxᵢ to zero gives λ̂=n/Σxᵢ=1/x̄.

items.stem: For n>1 observations from an exponential distribution with rate λ, the UMVUE of λ is:
items.explanation: The sum S=ΣXᵢ is complete sufficient and has Gamma(n, rate λ) distribution. Since E[(n−1)/S]=λ, this function of S is the UMVUE by Lehmann–Scheffé.

items.stem: If X₁,…,Xₙ are iid exponential(rate λ), then S=ΣXᵢ has which distribution?
items.explanation: A sum of n independent exponential variables with common rate λ has a Gamma distribution with shape n and rate λ.

items.stem: For S=ΣXᵢ from an iid exponential(rate λ) sample of size n, the pivot 2λS follows:
items.explanation: Since 2λXᵢ is χ²₂ for each exponential observation, summing n independent terms gives χ² with 2n degrees of freedom.

items.stem: The complete sufficient statistic for the rate λ in an iid exponential sample is:
items.explanation: The joint density factors through S=ΣXᵢ, making S sufficient. Its Gamma(n, rate λ) family is complete, so S is complete sufficient.

items.stem: For an exponential distribution parameterised by its mean θ, the maximum likelihood estimator of θ is:
items.explanation: The rate MLE is 1/x̄. Since θ=1/λ, invariance of maximum likelihood gives θ̂=x̄.

items.stem: For an iid exponential sample with mean θ, the sample mean X̄ is:
options: Always equal to the sample maximum
items.explanation: Each observation has expectation θ, so E(X̄)=n⁻¹ΣE(Xᵢ)=θ. Thus X̄ is unbiased for the population mean.

items.stem: For an iid exponential sample with mean θ and size n, Var(X̄) equals:
items.explanation: An exponential variable with mean θ has variance θ². Independence gives Var(X̄)=Var(X)/n=θ²/n.

items.stem: For X~Exponential(rate λ), the memoryless property is:
items.explanation: The survival function is e^(−λx). The conditional survival probability is e^(−λ(s+t))/e^(−λs)=e^(−λt)=P(X>t).
